phases.name: Inbox
phases.summary: Newly added links land here. Assign each a phase + priority.

phases.name: Immediate Wins
phases.summary: Quick, high-ROI upgrades to your existing projects that need zero new prerequisites. The aim is to make DocCluster meaningfully stronger and refresh your resume fast — reasoning-based RAG, faster embeddings, and bigger local models you can run on modest hardware.
phases.goal: Upgrade existing projects. Zero new prereqs. Fast ROI on resume.
phases.milestone: DocCluster v2: reasoning-based RAG + faster embeddings + bigger local model. Update resume.
concepts: Large local LLM inference on small GPUs (airllm)

phases.name: Plug Critical Interview Gaps
phases.summary: A 6.37 CGPA means interviewers probe hard, so these are non-negotiable before applying. You close the two biggest gaps: system design (nothing on the resume yet) and the math behind the attention variants you'll meet in papers.
phases.goal: CGPA 6.37 means interviewers probe hard. These are non-negotiable before any job applications.
phases.milestone: Can answer system design questions. Understand math behind attention variants.
concepts: System design fundamentals (caching, load balancing, consistent hashing, microservices)
Attention math, softmax, positional encoding (Jurafsky SLP3)

phases.name: Agent Foundations
phases.summary: Your biggest resume gap, closed: go from zero to understanding and building AI agents. You'll learn the agent-vs-workflow distinction, the core control loops, multi-agent patterns, and the production engineering (tools, context, evaluation) that separates a demo from a system.
phases.goal: Fill biggest resume gap. Go from zero to building agents.
phases.milestone: Understand agent architectures. Can describe in interview. Have run agent code.

phases.name: Research Papers
phases.summary: Amazon ML School showed you can read papers — this phase turns that into a high-signal skill for research and ML roles. You read four-plus papers on attention internals and efficiency, then study agent-harness engineering, and apply at least one technique (TurboQuant) to DocCluster.
phases.goal: Amazon ML School shows he can read papers. High-signal for research/ML roles.
phases.milestone: 4 papers read. Can discuss each technically. TurboQuant applied to DocCluster.
concepts: Long-running agent harness design (generator/evaluator, handoff artifacts)

phases.name: Build Agent Project
phases.summary: Convert everything you've learned into one strong, deployed agent project — worth more than ten tutorials. You'll use spec-driven development and multi-agent orchestration patterns, and set up real evaluation for the agent.
phases.goal: Convert learning into resume bullet. 1 strong agent project beats 10 tutorials.
phases.milestone: Deployed agent project on GitHub with README. New resume bullet.
concepts: Claude Code skills for solo builders (gstack)

phases.name: Trading AI Domain
phases.summary: An optional, high-paying niche where your ML background transfers directly. You study multi-agent trading architectures and the new financial foundation models, optionally building a small trading agent.
phases.goal: High-paying niche. His ML background transfers directly.
phases.milestone: Understand trading agent architecture. Optional: small trading agent project.

phases.name: Multimodal LLMs
phases.summary: Understand vision-language models end to end — from ViT patch embeddings to instruction-tuned VLMs — bridging your CNN background with modern multimodal AI. Culminates in a Multimodal DocCluster project.
phases.goal: Understand vision-language models end-to-end. From ViT patch embeddings to instruction-tuned VLMs. Bridge CNN background with modern multimodal AI.
phases.milestone: Can explain ViT/CLIP/BLIP-2/LLaVA architectures in technical interviews. Built Multimodal DocCluster project.

phases.name: Frontier Models and Architecture
phases.summary: Ongoing reference reading to stay current on models and architectures while you build. Dip in as needed rather than studying linearly.
phases.goal: Reference reading while building. Stay current on models and architectures.

phases.name: Claude Code Architecture (Optional)
phases.summary: Agent-harness internals — only worth your time if you branch into developer tooling. Reverse-engineered architectures and reimplementations of coding-agent harnesses.
phases.goal: Agent harness internals — only if branching into developer tooling.

links.title: CLIP (OpenAI)
links.description: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining — foundational vision-language model, zero-shot image classification via text prompts. Natural fit with his CNN/OpenCV background.

links.title: DINOv2 (Meta)
links.description: Self-supervised vision transformer — learns powerful visual features without labels. State-of-the-art on depth estimation, segmentation, classification. Pairs well with CLIP for multimodal projects.

links.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents (Anthropic)
links.description: Anthropic's engineering blog on designing harnesses for long-running agents — two-agent and three-agent architectures, progress logs, incremental session-based execution.

links.title: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
links.description: Decoder-only foundation model pre-trained on 12B K-line records from 45 global exchanges. Tokenizes OHLCV candlestick data into discrete tokens. +93% RankIC over leading TSFM. AAAI 2026.

links.title: How to Land a Frontier Lab Job
links.description: Practical guide on landing a job at frontier AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind) — portfolio strategy, referral networks, interview prep, mission-fit rounds

links.title: Intro to Agentic AI – Build Your First AI Agent
links.description: Hands-on intro to agentic AI: what agents are, how they reason, how to build your first agent using popular frameworks

links.title: Designing Agentic AI Systems for Enterprise Use-Cases
links.description: Production patterns for enterprise agentic AI: reflection, tool-use, multi-agent coordination, real-world projects (pricing agents, incident triage, recruitment systems)

links.title: How to Setup Evals For Agents
links.description: Practical guide to setting up evaluation pipelines for AI agents: automated evals, LLM-as-a-judge, DeepEval framework, CI/CD integration

links.title: Chronos (Amazon)
links.description: Pretrained language model for time series forecasting — zero-shot, probabilistic, 300+ forecasts/sec. Chronos-2 supports univariate, multivariate, and covariate-informed tasks. Pairs with TimesFM and Kronos.

links.title: Vision AI Learning Roadmap 2026
links.description: Complete 6-phase vision AI curriculum: CNN foundations → Vision Transformers → Detection & BEV → Self-supervised learning (DINO, MAE) → Video & world models → Multimodal AI (CLIP, SAM, LLaVA). Curated YouTube resources per topic.

links.title: Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN / BiFPN)
links.description: Multi-scale feature extraction for object detection — bottom-up + top-down pathways. BiFPN adds bi-directional weighted fusion (EfficientDet). Required for DETR understanding.

links.title: Swin Transformer
links.description: Hierarchical vision transformer with shifted windows — linear complexity, dense prediction backbone. SOTA on detection and segmentation. Yannic Kilcher video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SndHALawoag

links.title: DETR — End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
links.description: First transformer-based object detector — no anchors, no NMS, Hungarian matching. Direct ancestor of RF-DETR. Yannic Kilcher video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T35ba_VXkMY

links.title: Deformable DETR
links.description: Fixes DETR's slow convergence via deformable attention — attends to sparse key points not full feature map. Bridge between DETR and RF-DETR. Aleksa Gordić video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BNFNsLMlJqg

links.title: BEVFormer
links.description: Bird's Eye View representation from multi-camera images via spatiotemporal transformers. Tesla FSD-style multi-camera fusion. +9 NDS over prior SOTA on nuScenes.

links.title: Occupancy Networks (Tesla AI Day 2021)
links.description: 3D voxel occupancy prediction from camera-only input — Tesla's approach to 4D scene understanding without LiDAR. Covers Occupancy Network architecture and BEV planning.

links.title: DINO (original) — Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
links.description: Original DINO self-distillation paper (v1) — student-teacher ViT without labels. Emergent segmentation. Direct precursor to DINOv2. Yannic Kilcher video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h3ij3F3cPIk

links.title: MAE — Masked Autoencoders
links.description: Mask 75% of image patches, reconstruct pixels — BERT for vision. Kaiming He et al. (Meta). Data-efficient SSL baseline before DINOv2. Yannic Kilcher video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dp6iICL2dVI

links.title: SimCLR — Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning
links.description: Simple framework for contrastive learning — two augmented views of same image pulled together, different images pushed apart. Foundation for understanding CLIP contrastive training.

links.title: VideoMAE — Masked Autoencoders for Video
links.description: Extends MAE to video with tube masking (90% masking ratio). Data-efficient video understanding — trains ViT on small datasets. Tesla temporal stack prerequisite.

links.title: World Models for Autonomous Driving
links.description: Generative spatio-temporal neural systems that compress sensor observations into latent state and roll forward under actions — enabling vehicles to simulate futures. Curated paper list + GAIA-2 reference.

links.title: SAM — Segment Anything Model (Meta)
links.description: Universal image segmentation via point/box/text prompts — trained on 1B masks, 11M images. ViT backbone + lightweight mask decoder. SAM 2 extends to video.

links.title: LLaVA — Visual Instruction Tuning
links.description: First visual instruction-tuned VLM — CLIP visual encoder + LLaMA LLM + projection layer. Two-stage training: align then fine-tune. Foundation of GPT-4V style models.

links.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
links.description: Open-source RAG system combining knowledge graphs with dual-level retrieval for improved query comprehensiveness, diversity, and empowerment. EMNLP 2025. 67.6% vs 32.4% for NaiveRAG on agriculture domain.

links.title: ViT — An Image is Worth 16x16 Words
links.description: Original Vision Transformer — splits image into 16x16 patches, treats as tokens, feeds into standard transformer. Foundation for DINO, DINOv2, MAE, Swin, SAM, LLaVA. Read before any ViT-based paper.

links.title: Flamingo — Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
links.description: Bridges frozen vision encoder + LLM via cross-attention layers — interleaved image/text input, few-shot multimodal tasks. Single model outperforms fine-tuned task-specific models. DeepMind, 2022.

links.title: BLIP-2 — Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training
links.description: Lightweight Q-Former bridges frozen image encoder + frozen LLM. Outperforms Flamingo80B by 8.7% on zero-shot VQAv2 with 54x fewer trainable params. Salesforce, 2023.

links.title: InstructBLIP — Instruction Tuning for Vision-Language Models
links.description: Instruction-aware Q-Former on BLIP-2 — trained on 26 datasets, SOTA zero-shot on 13 held-out benchmarks. Standard architecture for generalizable VLMs. Salesforce, 2023.

links.title: Building Effective AI Agents (Anthropic)
links.description: Anthropic's engineering guide on agent design — workflow vs. agent distinction, the augmented-LLM primitive, five workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer), and autonomous agent loops with safeguards.

links.title: How we built our multi-agent research system (Anthropic)
links.description: Anthropic's production retrospective on Claude's Research feature — orchestrator (lead) agent spawning isolated parallel subagents, 90.2% gain over single-agent, prompt-engineering as primary lever, token-cost tradeoffs, and production hard parts (resumability, tracing, LLM-as-judge eval).

links.title: Writing effective tools for AI agents (Anthropic)
links.description: Anthropic's guide to designing, writing, and evaluating tools for LLM agents — tool-as-prompt, fewer workflow-shaped tools over 1:1 API wraps, namespacing, high-signal returns, input tolerance, and an eval-driven loop where Claude improves its own tools.

links.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents (Anthropic)
links.description: Curating the optimal token set during inference — context rot, right-altitude system prompts, just-in-time retrieval vs pre-loading, and long-horizon techniques (compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agents).

links.title: Harness design for long-running application development (Anthropic)
links.description: Multi-agent GAN-inspired generator/evaluator harness for multi-hour autonomous frontend/full-stack coding — three-agent design, context resets + structured handoff artifacts, verified completion gates. Companion repo: anthropics/cwc-long-running-agents.

links.title: How we built Claude Code auto mode (Anthropic)
links.description: Safer alternative to --dangerously-skip-permissions — a separate classifier model (Sonnet 4.6) reviews every action before execution, blocking unsafe ones while the agent recovers gracefully. Case study in runtime guardrail design for autonomous agents.
